name: Spirit of Inquiry: The Constitution Day Quiz
description:
This Constitution Day, join us, along with #ReclaimConstitution and QShala, for an evening of questions, stories and discoveries about India’s Constitution. Explore the people, ideas and unexpected connections behind the document that shapes our everyday lives—and win special prizes and Constitution memorabilia and goodies.

***Raghav Chakravarthy*** is a lawyer turned quizmaster and co-founder of QShala, a quiz and curiosity-based learning platform working with children, families, schools and institutions across India. Over the past decade, QShala has engaged more than 250 schools and built one of South Asia’s largest family quiz communities.

A National Tata Crucible Champion (2012), Raghav has designed and hosted over 500 quizzes across school, college, family and corporate formats. He has served as quizmaster for Conquest, one of India’s longest-running college quizzes on the Indian Constitution, and helmed AmiQuiz Curiae, an all-India quiz for lawyers.

He is also the author of *Ready for the Law Challenge*, published by Juggernaut.

name: Coro Off Duty x Where We Eat: Thanksgiving Supper
description:
There’s a moment at every good dinner when the table stops being a group of strangers. Someone asks for the bread. Someone else says you have to try this. By dessert, nobody remembers who knew whom.

This November, **Where We Eat is building that table**, and it's a long one.

Coro invited Where We Eat to Off Duty, their after-work evenings in Domlur, and Thanksgiving felt like the right reason to say yes. It’s a day built around a full table and saying thank you, and that’s always been the point of hosting for me.

The menu is European at heart, with quiet notes of Indian flavour. A pumpkin croqueta with charred pepper romesco. A tomato and pear carpaccio. Then a slow roast and braise for the table, with crushed potatoes, gur-glazed carrots and a green olive salsa verde. A hibiscus and orange palate cleanser. And to finish, a crepe cake layered with nolen gur cream.

Shared platters, a long table, and an evening that’s meant to run a little late.

*Please note that the food contains egg, dairy, nuts, gluten and cheese sauce that contains milk.*

What you get when you book:

- A recipe card from the menu, made with Gramiyaa wood-pressed oils, yours to take home and cook.
- Delicious Kombuchas from Local Ferment Co.
- A little something from the Where We Eat kitchen to yours.
- And most importantly, a table full of warmth, chatter and new faces.

The food is why you come. The people are why you’ll remember it.

description:
Be among the first in Bengaluru to experience Má Là Kitchen, a new restaurant bringing the flavours and culinary traditions of Sichuan to the city.

Some of the best food experiences begin around an intimate table, over a shared love for good food and the stories behind it. Má Là Kitchen is one such story.

What began as an intimate Sichuan supper club by Aditya Ramakrishnan with the help of his wife, Dongli Zhang, has now found a home of its own on 100 Ft Road, Indiranagar.

Rooted in the culinary traditions of Sichuan, Má Là Kitchen is an exploration of the region’s rich and layered food culture. The menu draws from Sichuan’s 24 recognised flavour profiles, bringing together traditional ingredients, time-honoured techniques and the distinctive interplay of heat, spice, fragrance and depth that defines the cuisine. Staying true to its origins, the food remains uncompromising in its approach, offering a taste of Sichuan without adapting its flavours to local palates.

Join Putting Scenes for a preview of Má Là Kitchen and get an early taste of the flavours, techniques and culinary traditions that make Sichuan cuisine so distinctive.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: The Curious Case of Sexual Normality
description:
**About the Lecture**

The Curious Case of Sexual Normality: Who decides what's deviant & what's desirable?

Our understanding of desire, pleasure, intimacy and sexual normality has always been influenced by the politics, cultural values and economic priorities of the societies studying them.

From psychoanalytic theories and sexual epidemics to India's alleged erotic histories and contemporary politics, author and independent researcher Tanisha Rao traces the fascinating history of how we study human sexuality.

Drawing on historical research, modern sexual science and personal accounts from her book You're Somebody's Kink, this lecture moves beyond the numbers to name those who benefit from a population’s lack of awareness, and the human beings whose intimate lives are shaped by them.

An exploration of the relationship between sexuality, science and society, the evening invites us to reconsider what we've been taught about sex, to question the assumptions we've inherited, and approach our own desires and differences with greater curiosity and compassion.

*Please note: Due to the sensitivity surrounding the topic of this lecture, we will be taking questions via paper chits contributed in a bowl and the speaker will be addressing them to the audience.*

**About the Speaker**

Tanisha Rao is a sexologist, sex coach and researcher whose work explores the intersections of desire, power, gender, shame and sexual culture.

She is the author of *You're Somebody's Kink* (2025), a nonfiction exploration of human desire beyond the conventional in contemporary India. Her research focuses on sexual fantasies, consent, masculinity, and power dynamics, with a particular focus on the evolving intimacies and sexualities of South Asians in a post-pandemic world.

Alongside her independent research, Tanisha works directly with individuals and couples as an intimacy coach, an experience that continually informs her research questions and deepens her understanding of the distance between established sexual knowledge and people's lived experiences.

Tanisha is the co-founder of *Sangya Project*, an Indian sexual wellness venture focused on challenging conventional pleasure and also writes an intimacy column for *Bombay Times*, where she brings together research, cultural criticism and insights from her practice to make complex conversations about sexuality more accessible.

**What to Expect:**

- A 60-minute lecture
- 30–45 minutes of interactive Q&A
- One kombucha included in your ticket

**Event Details:**

📅 Saturday, 28 November | 1 PM - 3 PM

📍 Atta Galatta, Indiranagar [near metro]

**About Pint of View**

Inspired by the successful Lectures on Tap community in the U.S., Pint of View brings this format to India for the first time. It’s where big ideas meet bar tables, and where you enjoy a drink in hand, walking out with a new way of seeing the world.

Book now & develop your own pint of view! 🍻

MEGHALAYA: MEAT. BBQ. ROCK & ROLL. TRIBAL CUISINE.

The LARGEST CONGREGATION of the meat masters of the country. Slow cooked meats over open fire - think whole hogs, assado grills and generations old smoking techniques brought to your city for one evening.

Meghalaya Fire & Feast rolls into town with a heavyweight line-up: BBQ legends, pitmasters and chefs from Meghalaya’s Khasi, Garo and Jaintia tribes, bringing smoked meats, glowing coals and a serious love for smoked meat.

On the grills: low-and-slow barbecue, meat over open flames and tribal recipes handed down through generations. These chefs have put in the hours. Come taste why they belong on this bill.

Cold beer pouring. Cocktails shaking. Motorcycles gleaming. Live bands tearing up the stage and DJs with unusual tastes and questionable respect for genre boundaries. Music curated by Harley Rock Riders, with the volume where it belongs.

Come hungry. Get close to the fire. Make some noise.

BURN, BABY, BURN.

name: Supa San | A Taste Of The New Japanese Izakaya
description:
Be among the first in Bengaluru to experience Supa San, the Japanese izakaya concept from Aditya Birla New Age Hospitality.

Inspired by the curiosity of a self-confessed super fan of Japanese culture, Supa San brings together the spirit of a neighbourhood izakaya with a playful world shaped by Japanese food, art and pop culture. The Bengaluru outpost takes this expression further through an illustrative, anime-inspired visual identity, bringing characters, collectibles and unexpected details into the space.

The experience moves across an expansive Japanese-inspired menu, from sushi, small plates and Robatayaki to bao, sando and comforting bowls of Kamameshi, Ramen and Mazemen. Join Putting Scenes for a table at Supa San and get an early taste of the food, drinks and culture shaping this new addition to Bengaluru's dining scene.
